title: Latency surge safeguard with regional egress cap and graceful handoff
author: Ethan Morales
description: Motivation: during a cross-region client rollout we observed short-lived latency spikes that caused regional egress queues to back up and trigger hard circuit trips, which then cascaded to upstream fallbacks and large request loss. This PR introduces a lightweight in-service safeguard that limits regional egress throughput when active latency surge patterns are detected and gracefully hands off traffic to secondary regions according to current routing policy. Design summary: 1) latency-surge-detector: a rolling p95/p99 slope detector that monitors per-region request latency and error-rate acceleration. 2) egress-cap-enforcer: when the detector crosses thresholds and error-budget consumption is high, we apply a soft token cap on regional egress for a short decay window (configurable, default 30s). 3) graceful-handoff: instead of hard-cut circuit trips, we mark the region as 'throttled' and bump routing weight to fallback regions using existing smart-routing hooks with a controlled ramp (10% steps every 5s) to avoid bulk failover. 4) operator controls: a new /admin/safeguard endpoint and a Helm toggle (values.safeguard.enabled) with override and immediate bypass for on-call. Config knobs: detector.window_ms=60000, detector.threshold.p99_surge=1.25, cap.window_s=30, ramp.step_percent=10, ramp.step_s=5. Rollout plan: canary to region-us-west-2 (10% traffic) for 24h, watch p99 latency, error_budget burn rate, and reroute_deltas. If stable, ramp to 100% and enable global default. Backout: disable values.safeguard.enabled or call /admin/safeguard/disable, which immediately removes cap and returns routing weights to baseline. Tests: unit tests for detector math, integration test simulating p99 surge with synthetic load solver, e2e scenario using perf-canary harness to validate no request loss during handoff. Metrics & dashboards: new metrics region.safeguard.state{region}=throttled/active/idle, region.safeguard.cap_tokens, region.safeguard.handoff_rate. Alerting: add SLO burn alert threshold when safeguard engages for >2m. Migration notes: no DB migration. Helm chart: new values and RBAC for /admin endpoints. Security: admin endpoint requires existing operator token; action audit log emitted to audit-log-exporter. Related: addresses ENG-9142 (reduce cascade from regional latency spikes), ties to SUP-1289 incident postmortem. Suggest a max_ramp_percent config.", "Author: Added max_ramp_percent with default 40 in commit 1b2e4d6; updated docs.", "Marco: Integration test passed locally but CI perf flagged a 3% p50 regression; is that expected due to additional checks?", "Author: Reduced detector allocation and moved critical path to lock-free read; perf bench re-run shows regression eliminated.", "Li: Please add a short operator note about audit logs and where to see handoff events.", "Author: Added audit note and dashboard link in runbook.", "Asha: Approved after nits fixed.", "Marco: Approved.", "Li: Approved."] CI checks: ["unit: pass", "integration: pass (flaky guard rerun)", "e2e-perf: pass (canary)", "lint: pass", "security-scan: pass"]. Observed behavior in canary: p99 reduced cascade trip incidents from 4/hour -> 0.5/hour during synthetic surge, end-to-end request success maintained at 99.98%. Release notes: "Add region-specific latency surge safeguard that applies soft egress caps and gradual fallback to prevent cascade failures; configurable via helm values.safeguard.*". Breaking change: "false". Additional notes: this PR is narrowly scoped to runtime request path and admin tooling; follow-up will add historical incident replay logs to better tune detector thresholds (ENG-9220).
